transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I’m just... exhausted. It's a kind of tired that sleep doesn’t really fix. Just getting through a normal workday and then managing dinner at home... it all just feels a lot heavier than it should lately.
How long have you been feeling this way—days, weeks, or longer?

I'd say it's been about a month. It's actually been a bit of a... a swing, I guess. Before this, I was feeling unusually energized and really driven at work, getting a ton done. But then it just shifted to feeling persistently low, and I've been stuck in this exhausted phase for the last four weeks or so.
During that period when you felt unusually energized and driven, did you find you needed less sleep than usual but still felt fine the next day?

Yes, exactly. During that stretch, I was sleeping maybe four hours a night. But I'd wake up feeling completely fine and just... ready to go. I'd be up early sending work emails, sketching out event ideas, or even just reorganizing the kitchen before anyone else was awake. It didn't seem to bother me at all at the time.

{"intent": "Determine whether this pattern of mood swings between elevated and low energy states has occurred repeatedly over a long period (to distinguish an episodic bipolar presentation from chronic cyclothymia)", "question": "Have you noticed similar swings between these energized, less-sleep periods and these low, exhausted periods happening repeatedly over the past couple of years, or is this the first time you've

I don't think so, no. I mean, I've always had busy weeks and slower weeks, but... I haven't noticed a repeated pattern like that over the last couple of years. This is really the first time it's been this noticeable—going from running on almost no sleep and feeling great, to just... completely hitting a wall. So, yeah, I'd say this is the first time it's happened quite like this.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly or that you seem to stop breathing or gasp for air while you're asleep?
No, my husband hasn't mentioned anything like that. He's usually a pretty light sleeper, so I think he'd notice if I was snoring loudly or gasping, but... no, he hasn't said anything.
Have you noticed any new sensitivity to cold, unexplained weight changes, or dry skin and hair over the past month?
No, not really. I mean, my weight has been pretty stable, and I haven't noticed feeling any colder than usual or having dry skin or anything like that. Everything seems pretty normal in that regard.
Have you noticed feeling unusually dizzy or lightheaded, or have your periods been heavier than usual lately?
No, I haven't noticed any dizziness or feeling lightheaded. And my periods haven't been any heavier than normal. They've been pretty much the same as they always are.
How many days in a row did that energized, low-sleep period last before it shifted into feeling exhausted and low?
I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. I didn't really keep track of the exact number of days. It just sort of... ran its course, I guess, and then I crashed. But I couldn't give you a specific number.
Have you noticed feeling unusually short of breath or your heart racing when climbing stairs or exercising, or has anyone commented that you look pale lately?

No, I haven't had any issues with that. I can take the stairs at work without getting winded or feeling my heart race. And, um, nobody has said I look pale, either. Everything's been pretty normal physically.
Thinking back, do you remember if that energized, less-sleep period lasted more like a few days—say under four—or did it go on for a week or more?
I really couldn't say for sure. Like I said, I wasn't keeping track. It might have been a few days, or it might have been closer to a week. I just know it happened, and then I crashed.
During that energized period, did people close to you—like your husband or coworkers—comment that you seemed noticeably different from your usual self?

Not that I can remember, no. My husband didn't say anything about me acting strange or anything. And at work... well, I'm a manager, so people are pretty used to me being busy and directing things. Nobody pulled me aside or made any comments about me being different. I think to them, I probably just seemed like I was having a really productive week.
During that energized period, did you find yourself making impulsive decisions—like spending more money than usual, taking on new commitments, or doing anything risky that wasn't like you?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I didn't go on any big shopping sprees or do anything dangerous. I was just getting a lot done at work and around the house. I don't really do risky things anyway, so... no, nothing like that stands out.
Even if you can't recall the exact number of days, do you feel fairly confident that the energized, low-sleep period lasted at least four days in a row?

I mean... yeah, I suppose so. If I had to guess, it was probably at least four days. Like I said, I wasn't marking it on a calendar or anything, but it definitely wasn't just a day or two. It felt like a solid stretch where I just didn't need much sleep and was constantly going. So, yes, four days seems pretty likely.
